items.title: Headlines for November 11, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## House GOP Blocks Impeachment Charges Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Nov 11, 2026 House Republicans on Tuesday blocked impeachment charges against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. By a margin of just seven votes, Republicans managed to bury the charges in committee through a 211-204 party-line procedural vote. Eleven Democrats skipped the vote, including Democratic Congressmember Nancy Pelosi of California. While House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is vying for the speakership in January, expressed support for Hegseth’s impeachment, many wondered how it was such a surprise that he was unable to corral Democratic votes to impeach Hegseth. President Trump hailed the outcome as an “exoneration.” Hours before the vote, Hegseth blasted the impeachment articles and said he’d carry out the same operations again. > Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth: “Let’s be clear about what this resolution actually does. It tells our enemies, Iran, the cartels, every adversary watching, that the United States will actually punish its own warriors and its own civilian leadership for successfully executing lawful military operations.” ... ## Rep. Jordan Elected as House GOP Leader as Senator Thune Reelected as Senate Republican Leader Nov 11, 2026 House Republicans elected Congressmember Jim Jordan, a staunch Trump ally, as their leader after last week’s sweeping midterm losses. Jordan will replace Speaker Mike Johnson come January when a new Democratic majority takes office with at least 256 seats in the House. In the Senate, Republicans reelected Senator John Thune of South Dakota as leader. Democrats currently have a 54-seat majority in the Senate, with the races in Alaska and Mississippi leaning toward Democrats. The Democratic Senate candidate in Mississippi, Scott Colom, leads his Republican opponent by 3,000 votes.

Despite those misgivings, immigration arrests have continued unabated. In Los Angeles, a line of immigration officers in masks and body armor blocked the entrance to a hospital emergency room in a heavily Latino neighborhood early Saturday. However, no major breakthroughs were announced in efforts to end the war that began nearly five years ago. The two-day session in Abu Dhabi was the first meeting in nine months. U.S. officials are determined to revive peace efforts, with envoys set to meet with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents. Fighting continues on the front line, with both countries using long-range missiles and drones. Ukrainian officials say three people were killed and 11 were injured after Russia launched a daytime attack on a market in the southern Odesa region. ## How Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affair could cause collateral damage in Washington WASHINGTON (AP) — Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, is under scrutiny after revelations of an affair with a Chinese businesswoman, Alice Huang, who is suspected of spying. Nvidia produces crucial AI chips that both China and the U.S. covet, and the affair has sparked concerns about national security. The Department of Justice is probing whether a company tied to Alice Huang, Megaspeed, illegally funneled chips to China. Nvidia's board says there's “no reason to believe” secrets were compromised. President Donald Trump, a supporter of Jensen Huang, has downplayed the issue. And China has denied the allegations that Alice Huang was a spy. ... ## As higher prices seep into broader economy, Fed officials consider faster hikes WASHINGTON (AP) — More evidence this week of hot inflation in the U.S. was unpleasant news for the Federal Reserve, not to mention consumers: Rising prices may be spreading beyond the one-time shocks from tariffs and high gas prices into the wider economy, meaning that mortgages, credit cards and other forms of borrowing are likely to become increasingly expensive. Tuesday’s consumer price index report showed broadly rising costs across a range of goods and services. There is increasing anxiety among Fed officials that higher oil prices stemming from the Iran war may last longer than previously thought. ... ## Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak BUNIA, Congo (AP) — Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, highlighting the severity of the situation. The health ministry reported on Wednesday 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths, making it Congo's deadliest outbreak. The crisis began in mid-May, and authorities have struggled to contain it due to armed conflicts, a health system crisis, poor roads, and violence fueled by mistrust. The Bundibugyo virus responsible for this outbreak has no known vaccine or treatment and has spread to eight provinces. Health workers face attacks, and experts urge more efforts to contain the disease, which has spread to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. ## World leaders urge stronger and faster action at UN climate talks over inadequate response ANTALYA, Turkey (AP) — World leaders were urged to act decisively to curb global warming as formal talkes opened Wednesday at the United Nations climate conference in Turkey. items.title: Fed officials open door to a quicker round of rate hikes as inflation worsens | live
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller's comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025.

items.title: AP Entertainment SummaryBrief at 4:48 p.m. EST | Features | rutlandherald.com
items.excerpt: - AP - Nov 11, 2026 - Nov 11, 2026 Updated 1 hr ago Rapper Yella Beezy convicted of hiring gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3 on busy Dallas interstate DALLAS (AP) — A Dallas County jury has unanimously convicted rapper Yella Beezy of capital murder in a brazen daylight attack on rapper MO3 on a busy Dallas interstate in 2020. Jurors found that Yella Beezy hired the gunman who fatally shot rapper MO3. Yella Beezy’s real name is Markies Conway, and MO3’s real name was Melvin Noble. The jury’s guilty verdict means the 35-year-old Conway will spend the rest of his life in prison without parole. Kewon White was found guilty in September of carrying out the fatal shooting and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Irma P. Hall, 'Soul Food' and 'The Ladykillers' actor who found fame at 60, dies at 91 Irma P. Hall, the beloved actress known for roles in “Soul Food” and “The Ladykillers,” has died at 91. Her family announced her passing Wednesday, though no cause was given. Hall was best known as Big Mama in “Soul Food,” a role that earned her an NAACP Image Award. She also received a Cannes Film Festival Jury Prize for her role in “The Ladykillers.” Hall's acting career began later in life after decades as a teacher. She was a dedicated member of her church and helped develop young artists. Her family remembers her as a woman of faith and a global teacher. The 'Hunger Games' are back, with an A-list cast and brutal origin story for Haymitch The “Hunger Games” franchise is back with “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” focusing on a young Haymitch Abernathy. Before becoming the mentor to Katniss and Peeta, Haymitch was a tribute from District 12. Director Francis Lawrence and producer Nina Jacobson cast a then-19-year-old Joseph Zada as Haymitch. Zada impressed with his charisma and mischief, essential for the role. The film's production spanned five months across Spain and Germany. The series has a lasting cultural impact, with over 100 million books sold and $3.3 billion in box office revenue. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson also return in the epilogue. Jordan Firstman has been a lot of things, but 'Club Kid' confirms he's a filmmaker NEW YORK (AP) — It’s taken some time but Jordan Firstman, with “Club Kid,” feels like he’s finally made it. Since its debut at the Cannes Film Festival, “Club Kid” has been a sensation. Now, he just needs to stay on his game. The film, which Firstman wrote, directed and stars in, draws from Firstman's own experiences with gay nightlife. His character is hard-partying, hard-drug user who's shocked to discover he has a 10-year-old son. After a bidding war, A24 picked it up for $17 million and is releasing the film in the heart of awards season. Firstman has been a provocative viral-video star, a TV series writer, an actor and more. But “Club Kid” confirms he's a filmmaker. Movie Review: James Gray delivers a milestone crime drama in ‘Paper Tiger’ Miles Teller and Adam Driver play brothers trying to work on a deal in 1986 New York in James Gray's “Paper Tiger.” Part crime drama, part family tragedy, the film also stars Scarlett Johansson as Teller's wife, Hester. All are trying to make a little more money in pursuit of their version of the American Dream. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr opines that “with an operatic grace and 35 mm grit, “Paper Tiger” shrewdly and authentically explores ideas about wealth, worth, the cost of family and price of wanting more.” Rated R, “Paper Tiger” opens in limited release Friday and expands nationwide Nov. 20. ... The 2027 Coachella lineup is here: Dua Lipa, Tame Impala and SZA to headline INDIO, Calif. (AP) — The 2027 Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival lineup is finally here. Dua Lipa, Tame Impala, and SZA will headline the event next April. Tame Impala, the musical project of Australian Kevin Parker, returns as a headliner after first topping the bill in 2019. SZA and Lipa have also performed at Coachella before. Daddy Yankee, set to be named artist of the year at the 2026 Latin Grammys, joins as a fourth headliner. The festival will feature Madonna, Phoebe Bridgers, and many more. Coachella returns to Indio, California, for two weekends in April 2027. Tickets go on sale Friday. ... Walliams and Brand were leading UK comics. Now they are part of a reckoning over sexual misconduct LONDON (AP) — A day after British actor-comedian Russell Brand was sent to prison for rape and sexual assault, allegations have surfaced against another leading comedian, David Walliams. The cases have sparked a wider reckoning about celebrity misconduct in the U.K. Walliams, a feted children's author and well-known TV personality, is facing allegations of using his fame to exploit young female fans. He had sought to block news organizations from publishing these claims, but a judge dismissed his bid. Walliams has not been charged, but the revelations have prompted questions about the media and entertainment industries' roles in enabling such behavior. Authorities are now urging stronger protections for women.
